conditions: SECAL I's second tranche required that state support to coal other than for mine closure and social protection fall by at least 40% in real terms in 1997; that at least one-third of coal support go to mine closure and social protection; and that no money for operating losses go to mines that hired more than 1% of their staff in a quarter. In the Kuzbass, Nezavisimaya Gazeta reported 17 mines shut since 1994, 17,000 people out of work and only 7% re-employed (via Green Left); a 1997 World Bank survey put the share at 24%.
